passages.original: Petrus primogenitus diaboli filius, et qui sanctæ Antiochenæ Ecclesiæ indignissime se ingessit, sanctamque sedem pontificatus Ignatii martyris pollnit, qui Petri dextra episcopus ordinatus est, Eustathiique confessoris ac praesidentis trecentorum decem et octo Patrum qui in Nicaea convenerunt, ausus est dicere non oportere Christum etiam Dei Filium nominare secundum di- vinam Salvatoris sanctionem et traditionem divinarum Scripturarum, Patrumque expositionem ; sed unum de Trinitate passionem pro nobis pertulisse in substantia deitatis, juxta Arii, Apollinaris, Eunomiique blasphemiam, volens hac voce evacuare salutarem Domini incarnationem , secundum quam Christus et passionem subiit. Dicitur autem et unus ex nobis, ut qui Abrahæ semen apprehendit (Hebr.
passages.english: Peter, the firstborn son of the devil, who most unworthily thrust himself into the holy Church of Antioch and has polluted the holy see of the pontificate of Ignatius the martyr, who was ordained bishop by the right hand of Peter, and of Eustathius the confessor and president of the three hundred and eighteen Fathers who assembled at Nicaea, has dared to say that one ought not to name Christ also the Son of God, according to the divine ordinance of the Saviour and the tradition of the divine Scriptures and the exposition of the Fathers; but [he says] that one of the Trinity endured suffering for us in the substance of the deity, following the blasphemy of Arius, Apollinaris and Eunomius, wishing by this expression to make void the saving incarnation of the Lord, according to which Christ also underwent suffering. But he is also called one of us, as he who took hold of the seed of Abraham (Heb.
passages.notes: 'pollnit' read as 'polluit' (has polluted); 'di- vinam' read as 'divinam'. The Peter meant is presumably Peter the Fuller, patriarch of Antioch, though the text names only 'Peter'. The passage breaks off mid-citation (Heb. 2[:16]), which the following context completes ('II)').
